name: Bunce Island
subtitle: Bunce Island is the site of the largest British slave castle on the Rice Coast of West Africa.

facts.label: What it was
facts.value: The largest British slave castle on the Rice Coast of West Africa

facts.label: Dates
facts.value: Founded around 1670; closed down by the British Parliament in 1808

facts.label: Operators
facts.value: Run by four London-based companies, including the Royal African Company

facts.label: Main owner
facts.value: Richard Oswald, principal owner in the 1750s, worked with South Carolina rice planter Henry Laurens

facts.label: Status
facts.value: National historic site under Sierra Leone's Ministry of Tourism and Monuments and Relics Commission

facts.label: Ruins
facts.value: Factory house, fortification, slave prison, watchtowers survive

facts.label: Preservation
facts.value: A US Park Service team issued a preservation management plan in 1989

facts.label: Pressure
facts.value: The government is trying to protect the island from coastal erosion and rising sea levels

parts.text: Bunce Island is the site of the largest British slave castle on the Rice Coast of West Africa. Founded around 1670, it was run by London companies until Parliament closed it in 1808. Substantial ruins remain, protected as a national historic site, and the government is trying to protect them from erosion and rising seas.
